Spatial accessibility and allocation modeling

Source: R/spax-package.R
spax-package.Rd

A modular engine for spatial access and allocation models. Floating catchment area (FCA) methods and an experimental static conditional logit allocation model with an outside option share the same demand, facility supply and travel inputs, optionally split into demand groups, the same decay kernels and one numeric engine. The allocation model includes the Huff model, declared with huff_allocation, and extends it with an outside option for demand that goes elsewhere. It can be evaluated, fitted to observed use, compared and used for prediction and scenarios. Output meanings remain model-specific.

Choose a workflow

spax_2sfca, spax_e2sfca and spax_m2sfca remain supported public FCA entry points; compute_access is also retained. The experimental spax_3sfca and spax_huff2sfca add selection weights that divide each origin's demand among the facilities. These take raster demand and facility travel layers. Multiple supply columns produce independent accessibility indicators, not interacting resource constraints.

The experimental allocation interface runs a model in one call: spax binds a model specification (spec_clm or spec_huff, with a decay such as decay_gaussian) to data from prep_data, and fits it to counts declared with obs_flows or obs_totals, or evaluates it when every parameter has a value. spax_clm and spax_huff do the same from raw inputs.

Underneath, the six experimental allocation steps are prepare_allocation, clm_allocation, fit_allocation, evaluate_allocation, predict_allocation and bootstrap_allocation; use them for full control. They describe one static CLM system with one supply vector and an outside option; huff_allocation declares the same system without the outside option, the classic Huff model. The first five support Gaussian, exponential and power decay and kernels declared with decay_kernel (fitting needs a kernel that is smooth in sigma); bootstrap has the narrower scope below. Prediction, the bootstrap (bootstrap_fit), check_fit and compare_fits (also named check_allocation() and compare_allocations()) accept a result of spax() in place of the model and its fit. Broader feedback-model declarations and general-purpose inference are not part of this experimental interface.

Inputs, observations and support

Preserve facility and origin IDs on numeric inputs. Named axes align independently; unnamed inputs are positional. For FCA, travel layer names identify facilities. In the allocation route, only included positive demand contributes to fitted facility loads. Known zero, unknown and excluded demand remain distinct. Requested predictions have their own support: unknown travel is not the same as a known absent connection (Inf).

Declare compatible demand, supply and travel units and reference periods. The interface records declarations without converting units. Specify whether observations are event counts over a period or a stock such as registered caseload at a reference date; a model output does not determine that meaning. obs_flows and obs_totals fit with the Poisson loss by default; fit_allocation with given starts defaults to weighted SSE. Choosing the Poisson objective is not evidence for an observation law.

Allocation outputs and scenarios

For a valid choice denominator, allocation contains inside probabilities, rho is their row sum and flow is demand times allocation. utilization sums those modeled counts by facility. The outside category is not automatically unmet need. A attributes raw supply per demand opportunity and abar = A/rho attributes supply per inside contact when defined. These are not delivered service or hard capacity constraints. Check saved validity flags, especially for unsupported positive supply, unknown travel and zero choice denominators, before reporting or mapping.

Prediction uses saved facility loads and does not refit or update the system when requested origins or their demand change. For a supply scenario, prepare the changed system and evaluate it at selected parameters. Supply can change attraction, allocation and loads as well as capacity attribution. This is a model-based comparison, not a causal intervention estimate.

Conditional bootstrap scope

bootstrap_allocation requires a static CLM with a fitted outside mass (v0) and a decay kernel that is smooth in sigma, either built in or declared with decay_kernel. The supply elasticity beta may be fixed or fitted, and kappa and a fixed beta may be any positive values. It also requires complete whole facility counts and an unweighted built-in Poisson original fit. Declare the event, reference period and independent-facility sampling assumption explicitly. Non-overlapping registrations alone do not establish independence. Demand, travel, supply and the included network stay fixed while facility observation multiplicities are resampled. Every physical facility remains in the allocation network.

Conditional percentile intervals require an eligible original fit, a complete run of 399 attempts and at least 380 finite successful values per quantity. Refused and incomplete results remain inspectable. Failed attempts are not replaced; successful inner-boundary estimates remain in the distribution. Coverage was evaluated for Gaussian decay with fitted sigma and v0, in generated 80-origin/40-facility designs under tested fixed-input laws; other kernels and a fitted beta use the same procedure without a separate coverage study. This is not a universal coverage guarantee or validation of an application's observation law. Regional attributed capacity per demand is a fixed-input identity and has no bootstrap interval. No simultaneous spatial intervals are provided. See bootstrap_allocation for the full restrictions.

Compatibility and migration

Existing public FCA calls remain supported. Their independent supply columns and accessibility scores do not become CLM probabilities by changing function names. Normalization choices remain part of the FCA model specification. Internal feedback models are private, and a shared execution engine does not establish universal mathematical nesting among the models.

Corrected static CLM and the older private huff_decay route have different equations and output meanings. Do not reinterpret saved legacy outputs as corrected contact or count outputs. Older private fits may lack the compact source snapshot or metadata needed for prediction and reporting; regenerate them from verified inputs rather than renaming their classes. Named observation axes align to canonical input IDs. Custom loss arguments indexed by observations must already use that canonical order.

Save input declarations and support metadata with fitted results, preferably in an RDS bundle. CSV exports discard R attributes. Inspect saved results with coef, fitted, summary, plot and as.data.frame; these methods do not silently fit or bootstrap again. Record the package version, and the source commit when using a development version from the develop branch.

Installed guides and status

Version 0.3.0 is the first release that includes the experimental allocation interface, which may change in later versions. Package and function help are installed with the package. Use help(package = "spax") to browse them. Installations with built articles also expose browseVignettes("spax"). Start with vignette("spax", package = "spax"), which computes one FCA surface; vignette("cornwall-data", package = "spax") describes the bundled Cornwall GP example data. The allocation workflow, vignette("allocation-workflow", package = "spax"), fits the model to the Cornwall GP registrations and covers prediction, a supply scenario, maps, export and fresh-session save/reload. The conditional bootstrap, vignette("facility-bootstrap", package = "spax"), uses a generated network.
